"Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit the field sampling across fans.** The requirement tightens with n (Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n, ΔB ∝ B²/n), so a sampling fine enough for an n≤4 fan undersamples an n=10 firming fan (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14, uniform-B at ΔB=0.1 T: 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T, where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening the field sampling. **Dynamic-range check, at design time**: a fan reads through one *fixed* sensitivity, so the scale must clear the **global worst corner**, structurally **low n × high B** — R ∝ 1/n on the gate axis stacks with the B-axis MR (10–100× zero-field). Size full-scale with **headroom, not precision** — saturation is the asymmetric failure: **better to lose low-resistance resolution than saturate** (expert practice). Set the scale comfortably above I_bias·R(n_min, B_max), anchoring R_max from a spot-check/CNP R-anchor × the **low-n** MR factor (MR grows toward CNP; a high-|n| factor under-sizes the corner — our-measurement). **Clipping distorts, it does not drop**: a railed column is flat-topped → harmonics + corrupted bg-subtraction across its whole FFT, unrecoverable by any B-window (the clean data sits at low B, the clip at high B). **Cost-floor check, at design time**: propose **exactly one** fan — the cheapest that clears the two checks above and delivers the claim. If the carrying tone is `censored`, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan. `SdhOnsetError` means no usable oscillations — re-examine the spot check, do not guess a `B_lo`; (2) **`n_max` = the validity window of the claim**; (3) `N_n` = its ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`; (4) `B_max` = the claim (more periods sharpen tones, but `B_max` past what the claim needs is just cost). `n_max` is the most expensive lever — out-of-validity it pays on *both* `N_B` and `N_n` (`Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n_max`). State the computed `N_B`, `N_n`, and wall-clock in the proposal.
27	2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. 28	3. Set the sensitivity (from the step-1 dynamic-range check) and time constant as an explicit pre-cell, fixed for the whole fan. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)`. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
29	4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
30	5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. 31	6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).

# Landau fan

## What
2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
```python
s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
```
Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.

## When
Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.

Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).

A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.

An undersampled axis produces in-data aliasing that mimics curved structure and survives re-plotting; no post-hoc check fully recovers it. "Start coarse" applies to the *window*, never below the Nyquist floor of the structure you intend to claim — and where the cost model says fine B is nearly free (blocking ramp-limited magnets), take it. **Re-run this check whenever n_max changes — never inherit the field sampling across fans.** The requirement tightens with n (Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n, ΔB ∝ B²/n), so a sampling fine enough for an n≤4 fan undersamples an n=10 firming fan (our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-14, uniform-B at ΔB=0.1 T: 2.2 rows/period at n=4 but only 1.5 — under the ≥2 floor — at n=10, B=4 T, where a spurious high-n second pocket appeared and had to be killed post-hoc). Where the rig makes fine B *not* free (measurement-dominated fans, e.g. a non-blocking-magnet rig at >1 s/pt — check the cost model), buy the high-n Nyquist floor by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n claim at B ≥ 5–6 T**, not by coarsening the field sampling. **Dynamic-range check, at design time**: a fan reads through one *fixed* sensitivity, so the scale must clear the **global worst corner**, structurally **low n × high B** — R ∝ 1/n on the gate axis stacks with the B-axis MR (10–100× zero-field). Size full-scale with **headroom, not precision** — saturation is the asymmetric failure: **better to lose low-resistance resolution than saturate** (expert practice). Set the scale comfortably above I_bias·R(n_min, B_max), anchoring R_max from a spot-check/CNP R-anchor × the **low-n** MR factor (MR grows toward CNP; a high-|n| factor under-sizes the corner — our-measurement). **Clipping distorts, it does not drop**: a railed column is flat-topped → harmonics + corrupted bg-subtraction across its whole FFT, unrecoverable by any B-window (the clean data sits at low B, the clip at high B). **Cost-floor check, at design time**: propose **exactly one** fan — the cheapest that clears the two checks above and delivers the claim. Compute `N_B · N_n · t_pt` and set each lever to its floor. **Do not offer a cheaper alternative or defer the trim to the operator — the floored design *is* the proposal.** Levers, in order: (1) **`B_lo` = the measured onset from `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B).onset_b` — compute it, do not eyeball it** (sub-onset rows are background, not signal; a too-low `B_lo` inflates both the 1/B span and the n-axis Nyquist, and eyeballed onsets run systematically too low). If the carrying tone is `censored`, the spot-check record never captured the onset — `onset_b` is that record's low edge, a valid lower bound for `B_lo`; a cheap low-field extension pins it before committing a long fan. `SdhOnsetError` means no usable oscillations — re-examine the spot check, do not guess a `B_lo`; (2) **`n_max` = the validity window of the claim**; (3) `N_n` = its ray-Nyquist floor at `B_lo`; (4) `B_max` = the claim (more periods sharpen tones, but `B_max` past what the claim needs is just cost). `n_max` is the most expensive lever — out-of-validity it pays on *both* `N_B` and `N_n` (`Δ(1/B) ∝ 1/n_max`). State the computed `N_B`, `N_n`, and wall-clock in the proposal.
2. Build the fast axis: `ns = np.linspace(n_hi, n_lo, N); Ds = D0 * np.ones(len(ns)); Vtgs, Vbgs = calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. A non-uniform n-vector is legitimate when you know where the action is — RPL_19's elevated-T fan stitches `np.hstack((n1, n2, n3))` with the dense segment over the CSC window and coarse segments elsewhere, with `#`-comments labeling each segment (20260124 cell 239).
3. Set the sensitivity (from the step-1 dynamic-range check) and time constant as an explicit pre-cell, fixed for the whole fan. RPL_19/20260217 cell 124 is the idiom: `sr830_N.sensitivity(10e-3)`, `sr830_N.time_constant(300e-3)`. Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` ≈ 4τ default — a Středa/dispersion fan tolerates the uniform fast-axis lag like a slope; ~6τ when the n-axis carries the extracted signal (per-column SdH FFT, or coarse n), where the lag distorts it, with denser n trading against the dwell.
8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.

## Verify
Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, plot_raw, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].

# 0. Raw view FIRST — one gain-divided pcolormesh per channel, no log, no
#    background removal. Rails/clipping, dead channels, streaks, and row
#    jumps are visible here and hidden by every derived (FFT/Středa) view.
plot_raw(run)

# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"

# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
B = run.col("magnet_field")
print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")

# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"

# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
#    events). Column name varies by era: 'T' (20260124-era RPL_19 has probe
#    + fridge both named T — col() takes the first), T_probe/T_fridge later.
for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
    if tname in run.cols:
        T = run.col(tname)
        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
        break

# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
for name in set(run.cols):
    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
        x = run.col(name)
        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
```

**Středa read** (the point of the fan): track ρxx dip positions n_dip(B) per B-row and fit dn/dB per dip family.
- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.

## Examples
- `aaron/RPL_10/241230_measure.ipynb` cells 50–53 — the original fans, exemplary comment discipline. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the index synopsis lumps these under "n-vs-B sweeps at D = 0.31" (cells 49–53); within that, cell 51 is a strict 1D field sweep (claimed by `field-sweep-1d` Examples, which already flags 50/52/53 as "landau-fan-shaped") and cell 54 is a *raw, never-executed* draft fan at D = 0.25. The executed fans: cell 50 → file 156 (101 B × 101 n, B 1→0 T, `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1`, 4.3 h), cell 52 → file 158 (351 × 201 — **interrupted at 0.0 h** and immediately superseded), cell 53 → file 159 (351 × 251, 27.8 h, the fan the qo-discovery fixture freezes on). Note B runs *downward* (1→0): the magnet was parked at 1 T by the preceding `## Gate maps in field` cells 46–48, so the fan starts where the magnet sits.
- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 117–119, 173–176, 234–242, 278–284 — the mature fan family. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the brief cited the "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" as ~cells 167–176; actually 167–172 are still `# Resuming effective mass` (higher field range), the small-fan section is header 173, base-recool cell 174 (`heater.volt(0)` + 1 h `interruptible_sleep`), fans 175 (D = 0.2) and 176 (D = 1) — 161 B steps 0.9→2.5 T × 151-pt n-line, `fast_delay=0.6` → file 1776, 5.5 h, the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture cut. Cell 119 is the first `## Test fan` (501 × 51, B 0.75–1.25 T at 1 mT steps). Cells 234–242 are the deep fan (cell 236 → file 1840: 441 × 231, 0.6→5 T, 30.1 h) plus the `## Elevated T Fan` (heater at 2.75 V, 20-min settle, designer hstack n-vector, ±5 T in four chained segments). - `aaron/RPL_19/20260217_measure.ipynb` cells 87–96 and 123–126 — fans with explicit field-settle and lock-in-setup cells. Cells 88/91/94 are `s.ramp(mag.field, B); time.sleep(600)` positioning cells; cell 89 presets sensitivity; cells 90/92 are 201 × 101 CSC fans at D = 1.02/0.98 (2.5→0.5 T); cell 95 is the 12 T fan (5→12 T, 351 × 201); cell 96 descends 12→0 with the two-density hstack `field_vec`. ## Next

1	# SdH spot check
2	
3	## What
4	A fixed-(n, D) magnetic-field sweep over a **low-field window**, designed to resolve
5	Shubnikov–de Haas / quantum-oscillation **frequency content** at one density — the
6	onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
7	`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
8	makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, 1/B spacing
9	Δ(1/B), and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B
10	FFT.
11	It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
12	quality**.
13	
14	## When
15	- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
16	  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
17	  Δ(1/B)), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
18	  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
19	  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
20	- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
21	  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.
22	
23	## Why
24	A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
25	low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
26	Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
27	noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:
28	
29	- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
30	  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
31	  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
32	  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
33	  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
34	- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
35	  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
36	  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
37	  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
38	  when the target is a weak tone.
39	
40	## Recipe
41	1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
42	   clearest tones. Sweep a field window **[B_lo, B_hi]**; the sampling grid follows
43	   the magnet class:
44	   - **Field moves cheap** (non-blocking magnet): sample **uniformly in 1/B**
45	     (`field_invB`) — constant points-per-period, FFT the raw points (no resample).
46	     `B_lo` is a small positive floor (~0.1–0.3 T) below the expected **onset** (the
47	     lowest B where oscillations emerge once the MR background is subtracted) —
48	     uniform-1/B is densest in B at low field, so it captures the onset for free.
49	   - **Blocking rate-limited magnet** (traverse dominates wall-clock): sample
50	     **uniformly in B** with **ΔB = Δ(1/B)·B_lo²** (Nyquist held at the low-B edge;
51	     `sdh_fft` resamples internally). Same wall-clock — the points ride the traverse —
52	     with ≳30× the per-period averaging at high B and no blind ramps between sparse
53	     high-B points. ΔB scales as B_lo², so put `B_lo` just below the expected onset,
54	     not at a deep floor.
55	2. **Δ(1/B) from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and Nyquist-resolve it: Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L)
56	   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1 uniform-1/B,
57	   N = (B_hi − B_lo)/ΔB + 1 uniform-B. This Δ(1/B) (and N) is what a committed fan
58	   inherits.
59	3. **δF from the record.** The tone resolution is set by the usable 1/B record above
60	   onset: **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** — tones closer than ~δF merge; trust a
61	   split only past ~2·δF. On high-T_e rigs the onset, not the field cap, sets δF:
62	   once 1/B_max ≪ 1/B_onset, raising B_max buys little — the lever is the
63	   density/side with the lower onset. Compute δF against the tones the claim must
64	   separate before sweeping.
65	4. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
66	   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
67	   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
68	5. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
69	   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field, B_vec,
70	   delay=dwell)` with the step-1 grid, fp the temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P,
71	   plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
72	6. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias).
73	   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` is
74	     the low-B edge of usable oscillation content (minimum over the tracked tones —
75	     a light tone that outlives the dominant one carries it), `clip_high_b` the high
76	     edge. `tones` holds each tone's own track: `freq`, per-tone `onset_b`,
77	     `snr`/`amp` curves over `b_centers`, `delta_f(b_max)` (that tone's usable-record
78	     resolution), and flags — `censored` (still above threshold at the record's low
79	     edge: `onset_b` is the record edge, not a measured die-off), `revived`,
80	     `marginal`, `near_residual`, and the bidirectional harmonic pair
81	     `harmonic_of` (this tone sits at k× a lower tone) / `harmonics` (freqs of
82	     tones sitting at k× of this one — a comb member is flagged from both ends
83	     regardless of which is stronger). Print `on.summary()` in the read
84	     cell. Pass `r_full_scale = sensitivity / I_bias` so a soft-clipped channel
85	     truncates the analysis window (with a warning) instead of feeding a flat-topped
86	     record to the FFT. Failure raises `SdhOnsetError` naming what was untrackable —
87	     that is a read result (no usable oscillations), not a prompt to eyeball.
88	   - **FFT** — `hera.analysis.sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=(cutoff, B_max), bg_degree=5)`
89	     takes `R_grid` as `(n_B, n_fast)` — pass a single trace as `R[:, None]` — removes
90	     the MR background with a degree-`bg_degree` polynomial **in B** (the background is
91	     smooth in B, not 1/B), then FFTs in 1/B per column, and returns
92	     `(freqs, spec[n_fast, n_freq])` with `freqs` in Tesla. It needs a field range wide enough that
93	     the polynomial captures the background without absorbing the oscillations.
94	     `cutoff ≥ onset_b`, and often **above** it (Verify). Read the **tone frequencies**
95	     against F_L.
96	
97	## Verify
98	- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
99	  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
100	  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
101	  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
102	  strong signal.
103	- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If Δ(1/B) under-samples the
104	  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
105	  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
106	  (worked case: Examples).
107	- **Grid-change reproduction separates tones from aliases.** A real tone survives a
108	  change of sampling scheme (uniform-B vs uniform-1/B); an alias moves with the grid.
109	- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary `bg_degree` and the window; a real peak **sharpens**
110	  as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
111	- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
112	  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed), not

114	  residual background near the low-B end inflates the slowest tones, so raise the cutoff
115	  above the onset until the slow-tone amplitudes stop shrinking. Report the onset — it
116	  sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (a rise on a later cooldown is a
117	  device-quality regression).
118	
119	## Examples
120	- *(our-measurement)* — a fine-step spot check resolved two tones (a main tone + a
121	  low-frequency partner), where a same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and
122	  under-settled did not. An earlier 4× coarser step had under-sampled the main tone,
123	  folding its aliases into the small-tone band. The worked case for "acquire the
124	  spot check well, *then* commit the fan."
125	
126	## Next
127	- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's
128	  Δ(1/B), settling, and onset; or take a couple more spot checks across density for a
129	  cheap preview of the n-dependence.

131	  FS-count combinatorics).
132	- **Tone amplitude vs T wanted** (effective mass) → `temperature-dependence`
133	  Flavor B.

**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute
frequencies.** The discriminating outputs are the FS count, the ABAB partition
and its φ²-split masses, and the model-independent Luttinger sum
Σ±f = (h/4e)|n|. Absolute frequencies inherit the hopping-parameter error bars.

- **ABAB**: Koshino–McCann graphite SWMcC set {γ₀ = 3.0, γ₁ = 0.4, γ₂ = −0.02,

    The denominator is the *measured* drain current `I = X_cur / gain_cur`
    (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a nominal bias
    current. Gains come from `measurement_config` (shared `resolve_channels`);
    nothing is hardcoded. Returned R is **signed** (X/I) — take `np.abs` for

    voltage channels returned (the current channel is always resolved).

# Spot-check analysis: runs 6 (electron, n=+3.2e12) and 7 (hole, n=-1.2e12)
# Raw MR + sdh_onset + sdh_fft, tones vs F_L and the fs_count model.
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import (open_run, summarize_run, sdh_onset, sdh_fft,
                           luttinger_frequency, resolve_channels, SdhOnsetError)

BASE = "/home/hera/measurements/zack/20260822-vti-02/data"
OUT = "/home/hera/measurements/zack/20260822-vti-02/hera_scratch"

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 8))

for row, (rid, nval, tag) in enumerate(((6, +3.2e12, "electron"), (7, -1.2e12, "hole"))):
    run = open_run(f"{BASE}/{rid}")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"RUN {rid} ({tag}, n = {nval:+.2e} cm^-2)")
    B = run.col("magnet_field")
    chans = resolve_channels(run.meta["measurement_config"])
    print("channels:", [(c.name, c.gain, c.role) for c in chans])
    g = {c.name: c.gain for c in chans}
    I = run.col("sr0_X") / g["sr0"]          # measured drain current, A
    V = run.col("sr1_X") / g["sr1"]          # Rxx voltage, V
    R = V / I
    # sort ascending in B (run 7 descends)
    idx = np.argsort(B)
    B, R, I = B[idx], R[idx], I[idx]
    Ib = np.median(np.abs(I))
    print(f"I_bias measured (median |I|): {Ib*1e9:.3f} nA;  R(B~0) = {np.median(np.abs(R[:10])):.1f} ohm; R range {np.nanmin(R):.1f}..{np.nanmax(R):.1f}")
    F_L = luttinger_frequency(abs(nval) * 1e4)  # cm^-2 -> m^-2
    print(f"F_L = {float(F_L):.2f} T")

    r_fs = 50e-6 / Ib   # sr1 sensitivity 50 uV fixed for both runs
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=r_fs)
        print(on.summary())
        onset = on.onset_b
    except SdhOnsetError as e:
        print("SdhOnsetError:", e)
        on, onset = None, None

    # raw MR
    ax = axes[row, 0]
    ax.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("Rxx (ohm)")
    ax.set_title(f"run {rid} {tag}: raw Rxx(B)")
    if onset:
        ax.axvline(onset, color="r", ls="--", lw=0.8)

    # background-subtracted dRxx
    ax = axes[row, 1]
    sel = B > 0.5
    p = np.polyfit(B[sel], R[sel], 5)
    dR = R[sel] - np.polyval(p, B[sel])
    ax.plot(B[sel], dR, lw=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("dRxx (ohm)")
    ax.set_title("bg-subtracted (deg 5)")

    # FFT above onset
    ax = axes[row, 2]
    if onset:
        cutoffs = [onset, onset * 1.15, onset * 1.3]
    else:
        cutoffs = [1.5, 2.0, 2.5]
    for co in cutoffs:
        try:
            f, spec = sdh_fft(R[:, None], B, b_range=(co, float(B.max())), log=False)
            s = spec[0] / np.nanmax(spec[0])
            ax.plot(f, s, lw=0.8, label=f"cutoff {co:.2f} T")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"fft cutoff {co:.2f}: {e}")
    ax.axvline(float(F_L), color="k", ls=":", label=f"F_L={float(F_L):.1f} T")
    ax.set_xlim(0, float(F_L) * 1.6)
    ax.set_xlabel("F (T)"); ax.set_ylabel("FFT amp (norm)")
    ax.set_title("SdH FFT in 1/B")
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/spot_checks_runs67.png", dpi=110)
print("saved", f"{OUT}/spot_checks_runs67.png")

import numpy as np
import scipy.constants as cst
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from pathlib import Path

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run,
    plot_raw,
    summarize_run,
    fan_grids,
    resistance_grids,
    sdh_fft,
    GateCalibration,
    luttinger_frequency,
)

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))

"""Runs 6-7 raw view: SdH spot checks at D = 0 (`sdh-spot-check`).
Run 6: electron n = +3.2e12, B 0 -> 10 T (50 mT to 1 T, 10 mT above), sr1 50 uV.
Run 7: hole n = -1.2e12, B 10 -> 0.3 T ride-down, 20 mT, sr1 50 uV.
Gain-divided Rxx = (sr1_X/1) / (sr0_X/-1e6) from the TSV, no background removal."""
from hera.analysis import resolve_channels


def spot_trace(rid):
    r = run(rid)
    gains = {c.cid: c.gain for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / gains["sr0"]            # measured drain current, A
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / gains["sr1"]) / I      # signed Rxx, ohm
    o = np.argsort(B)                            # run 7 descends; sort ascending
    return B[o], R[o], I[o], r


R_FS_50UV = 50e-6 / 9.9e-9  # 50 uV sensitivity at the measured ~9.9 nA bias = 5.05 kOhm

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.5, 3.8))
for a, (rid, lab) in zip(axs, ((6, "run 6 — electron, n = +3.2e12, D = 0"),
                               (7, "run 7 — hole, n = −1.2e12, D = 0"))):
    B, R, I, r = spot_trace(rid)
    print(summarize_run(r))
    a.plot(B, R, lw=0.6)
    a.set_xlabel("B (T)"); a.set_ylabel(r"$R_{xx}$ ($\Omega$)"); a.set_title(lab, fontsize=10)
    print(f"run {rid}: complete={not r.interrupted}; I_bias {np.median(np.abs(I))*1e9:.2f} nA; "
          f"R(B~0) {np.median(np.abs(R[:10])):.0f} Ohm; max|R| {np.abs(R).max():.0f} Ohm "
          f"= {np.abs(R).max()/R_FS_50UV*100:.0f}% of the 50 uV full scale (no clipping)\n")

from hera.analysis import resolve_channels


def spot_trace(rid):
    r = run(rid)
    gains = {c.cid: c.gain for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field")
    I = r.col("sr0_X") / gains["sr0"]            # measured drain current, A
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / gains["sr1"]) / I      # signed Rxx, ohm
    o = np.argsort(B)                            # run 7 descends; sort ascending
    return B[o], R[o], I[o], r

**Read (runs 6–7).**

**Run 6 (electron, F_L = 33.1 T) — clean two-tone constellation, decisive for the fan design but not yet for the call.** A strong light tone at **7.1 T** (SNR ≈ 40 at the record's low edge — onset *censored*, ≤ 0.3 T) with harmonics at 14.1 / 29.5 T, and a tone at **22.1 T** (onset 1.36 T, SNR 37). The 22.1 T tone is flagged `~3×7.1`, but discarding it as a harmonic breaks the partition sum — exactly the trap the investigation names (the ABAB ratio drifts through 3× with density): **7.1 + 22.1 = 29.2 T = 0.88·F_L** with partition **0.24/0.76**, against the ABAB model's 0.22/0.78 at this density — i.e. an ABAB pair at a global density scale of 0.88, inside the lever-arm prior (0.8–1.2). Fork, to be decided on n-dependence: (a) ABAB pair (heavy tone follows its own Onsager curve, diving light tone at low n), vs (b) single 7.1 T pocket + 3rd harmonic (22.1 tracks 3×f₁ exactly). The remaining low-F censored tones (3.0, 4.2, 5.1, 9.5 T) sit near the residual-background band and don't sharpen across the cutoff ladder — treated as background leakage, not pockets, pending the fan.

**Run 7 (hole, F_L = 12.4 T) — the predicted near-CNP exception regime, not decisive.** Crowded set: 4.7 and 6.6 T (sum 11.3 = 0.91·F_L; model ABAB pair 5.9/6.5 — close and balanced), plus unassigned 8.5 and 12.3 T and harmonic combs. Beat-like and unresolvable at this density per the investigation's stated low-|n| exception; the hole side reaches only |n| = 1.27×10¹² inside the gate limits, so it cannot be pushed into the separated regime.

**Both sides tell a consistent global-scale story (~0.88–0.91), and both show multi-tone content — no clean ABCA singleton on either side so far.** Side call for Step 4: **electron** — lower onset (≤ 0.3 T vs 0.71 T), separated tones, and design densities |n| ≥ 2×10¹² reachable (up to +3.27×10¹² on the D = 0 line). Handed to the fan: B_lo = 0.3 T (censored onset lower bound), tone band to Nyquist ≤ 33 T (coherent content observed up to 32.4 T, ≤ 7% noise-floor level above 36 T), sensitivity 50 µV (worst corner measured directly by run 7: 587 Ω at |n| = 1.2×10¹², 10 T = 12% FS), settling τ = 0.3 s.

## HERA — Step 4: Landau fan, electron side at D = 0 (`landau-fan-vti`) — the stacking-call dataset

**Why this fan (investigation Step 4, inheriting run 6/7 spot checks — see ana).** Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹²) left a fork the n-dependence decides: 7.1 + 22.1 T sum to 0.88·F_L with an ABAB-like 0.24/0.76 partition, but 22.1 ≈ 3×7.1 — real heavy pocket vs 3rd harmonic. Across the fan a harmonic tracks 3×f₁ exactly, a real heavy tone follows its own Onsager curve (model: light tone dives 7.3 → 1.1 T over n = 3.2 → 1.2×10¹² while the heavy tone stays near F_L) — the trajectories diverge unmistakably. Hole side stays a preview (run 7): gate limits cap it at |n| ≤ 1.27×10¹², inside the model's balanced-pair exception regime — a hole fan would be uninformative, that's the coverage trade.

**Design (computed, `landau-fan.md` step 1 + VTI variant cost regime):**
- **Fast axis**: n = +3.2 → +1.2×10¹² cm⁻² at D = 0 (run-5 cal), **141 pts** (Δn = 1.43×10¹⁰ ≤ half the ray spacing 2.90×10¹⁰ at B_lo = 0.3 T). Vtg +0.984 → +0.411, Vbg +1.166 → +0.425 V — inside validators. n_min = 1.2×10¹²: the ABAB partner needs ≥5 periods, resolvable only for n ≳ 1.35×10¹² (model f_partner); below that columns are exception-regime background — the low-n claim floors there.
- **Slow axis**: **B 10 → 0.3 T uniform in 1/B, Δ(1/B) = 0.0121 T⁻¹ → 269 rows.** Nyquist 41.3 T covers the coherent content observed in run 6 (≤ 32.4 T; ≤7% noise-floor above 36 T) with 2.5× margin on F_L(n_max) = 33.1 T. δF = 0.31 T over the 0.3–10 T record; the binding split (22.1 vs 3×7.1 = 0.8 T) is 2.6·δF. B_lo = 0.3 T = run 6's censored onset lower bound (raising it would kill the harmonic-vs-heavy split; lowering it inflates both axes' floors).
- **Direction**: descending — magnet pre-ramps 0 → 10 T (bare, blocking, ~73 min), fan rides home 10 → 0.3 T and **ends at 0.3 T**. This puts the worst dynamic-range corner (n = 1.2×10¹² × 10 T, measured by run 7: 587 Ω = 12% of FS) **in the first row** — the cheapest possible kill for a sensitivity mistake — and lands the FFT-grade high-B record in the first ~3 h instead of the last.
- **Sensitivity/settling inherited from the spot checks**: sr1 50 µV (5 kΩ FS), τ = 0.3 s / 24 dB; fast_delay = 1.2 s (4τ — the retrace lag is static per column and removed by the per-column background; the residual n-smear is < δF; the 2026-06-14 VTI trilayer fan idiom), slow_delay = 1. Leak trip 1 nA.
- **Price** (calibrated: run 5 fast-axis 1.10 s/pt at fast_delay 1.0 → 1.3 s/pt here; runs 6/7 field overhead 3.08 s/row): pre-ramp 73 min + in-fan traverse 71 min + 269 settles 14 min + grid 269×141×1.3 s = 13.7 h + turnaround ~9 min ≈ 16.4 h; realistic **~17.5 h**.

**Checkpoints** (hera-watch armed on the run dir): (1) **first row ~75 min in** (after the pre-ramp): rail/clip across the full n-line at 10 T, leakage, both channels live; (2) **~4 h**: high-B record (B ≳ 2 T, rows 1–33) per-column FFT — heavy-tone F(n) trajectory, the early template read; abort/redesign if the 22.1 T tone is absent across all n; (3) every ~3–4 h: light-tone F(n) on the growing 1/B record, T_sample at base, leakage. Magnet ends at 0.3 T, gates park at 0.

magnet.field(float(B_vec[0]))

s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)

        station.interrupt_requested = True

    s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs],
